But it was rather curious that Philly closed the game with Dean Wade and Adem Bona splitting time at the five even though Joel Embiid was on the active roster for the night. Embiid left the game with 3:51 remaining in the third quarter and did not return to the game, and considering his lengthy injury history, this might have caused some 76ers fans worry. However, the 76ers star clarified that he simply did not suit up towards the end of their win over the Bulls since he was under a minutes restriction, as per Adam Aaronson of The Philly Voice. 76ers head coach Nick Nurse also seconded this, as he said that Embiid was “okay” and that limiting his minutes on the night was part of the team’s decision to help manage the foot issue he’s been dealing with. Considering how the 76ers are playing the long game, there is no surprise whatsoever that they are taking every opportunity they can to give Embiid some rest. They stacked the roster with the likes of Jaylen Brown and LeBron James to help ease the workload that Embiid has to take in in the regular season. Moreover, Tyrese Maxey has been brilliant all season long, and he had another stellar outing (26 points and 11 assists) to lead Philly. Embiid missed a total of 150 games over the past three seasons, and he is surely going to sit out all back-to-backs for the 76ers this year. But if he enters the playoffs fresh, that could make all the difference for Philly. item.description: EUGENE, OR - OCTOBER 31: Oregon Ducks wide receiver Jalen Lott (10) leaps for a pass against Northwestern Wildcats defensive back Montae Pate (4) during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Northwestern Wildcats on October 31, 2026 at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Brian Murphy/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images This was such a winnable football game. And that’s what stings so much. This wasn’t the type of game familiar to so many Northwestern fans — like when the 5-0 2015 ‘Cats suffered back-to-back 30-point losses to No. 18 Michigan State and No. 17 Iowa, or when the No. 18-ranked 2000 ’Cats were bashed 66-17 in the Alamo Bowl by No. 9 Nebraska. It wasn’t a game where a hopeful Wildcat team went on the road for a prove-it game against a top team just to get knocked on its back. Rather, David Braun’s squad affirmed in a lot of ways what Northwestern fans have been cautious about believing all season long: that this is a great football team. On the road, against Oregon — a certified college football juggernaut, no matter the struggles it is having this season — the ‘Cats jumped out to a 20-6 first-half lead and were FLYING on both side of the ball. Aidan Chiles, Griffin Wilde and Chip Kelly’s offense scored on each of its first four possessions and looked unstoppable, while the defense held Oregon to just 83 total yards on its first three drives. And then, that all disappeared. NU averaged just 4.5 yards per play the rest of the game, well below its 6.5 season average, and got rattled on the back end by Dylan Raiola and the Ducks’ receiving cast. And, before we knew it, the game had slipped from the ‘Cats’ paws. Here are three takeaways from Northwestern’s heartbreaking 34-26 Halloween loss in Eugene: 1. Backup defensive backs Ore Adeyi and Montae Pate were targeted by Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti throughout the evening, while also failing their assignments multiple times in run defense. On Saturday, it was persisting sub-par health in this unit that, once again, contributed in a big way to a Northwestern Big Ten road loss. item.title: Marist basketball unravels late, drops opener to Dartmouth
item.description: A nip-and-tuck affair had Marist coach John Dunne waiting anxiously for a breakaway surge in the season opener against Dartmouth . His Red Foxes finally pulled out to a nine-point lead midway through the second half. But instead of settling in, Marist unraveled and allowed Dartmouth to storm back into the contest with the Big Green ultimately winning 69-62 and spoiling a debut before 890 at McCann Arena in Poughkeepsie on Monday, November 2. A pair of free throws by Myles Parker with 10:53 left put Marist on top 47-38, the largest margin after an opening 23 minutes that was played was basically a 2-4 point affair. That's when the game turned: Marist missed nine of its final 12 shots and turned the ball over five times. Dartmouth surged with eight consecutive points and finally took the lead on a 3-pointer by Sam Civello with 5:52 left, a lead the Big Green never lost. "The first half was kind of expected; their pressure really affected us,'' Dunne said. "I thought we settled in for a little bit in the second half. Once we got that lead, I thought we were going to relax and take it from there. But give them credit; they battled, they take you out of rhythm." Marist finished with 18 turnovers, which Dartmouth turned into 14 points, and the Red Foxes shot 37 percent. Grad student Jadin Collins-Roberts hit all but one of a dozen free throw attempts, but his 1-for-9 field-goal shooting left him with just 13 points - he also had seven turnovers. Sophomore Myles Parker scored 13 off the bench. Freshman Dywane Chess and sophomore Jordan Gabriel each had eight. Edward Onyia had six boards. Dartmouth shot 45 percent and hit eight 3-pointers. Four double-digit scorers included Cameron McNamee (12), Anton Strelnikov (12), Camerton Hiatt (11) and Landon Williams (10). Marist will host Maryland-Baltimore County in the first America East-Metro Challenge game at 7 p.m. Thursday. item.title: Morgan boys soccer defeats Valley Regional to claim Shoreline Conference championship
item.description: The Morgan boys soccer team beat Valley Regional 3-1 to win the Shoreline Conference championship at Blythe Field Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (Joe Morelli / Hearst Connecticut Media) DEEP RIVER - Jayden Gutierrez had been to plenty of Morgan boys soccer games as a youth. He went to see his older brother Jonathan put on a show. Now Jayden is a freshman for the Huskies and already a key contributor. He has already accomplished something in a Morgan uniform that Jonathan never did. Jayden scored one of three goals Monday night to lead the fourth-seeded Huskies to a 3-1 victory over No. 6 Valley Regional for the Shoreline Conference championship. "This year, we were doubted a lot. We weren't expected to make it that far. Just how my brother did, we never gave up and we kept going," Jayden Gutierrez said. The Huskies (11-5-2) reached a pair of Shoreline finals in 2022 and 2025, but came up short in both games. This is the first solo Shoreline title for Morgan since 2018. The Huskies were co-champions in 2019 and 2021. Jonathan Gutierrez earned All-American honors last season and is now playing at the University of Hartford. "We lost six all-conference players with an All-American and a couple all-state players. We knew going in we had to put the puzzle pieces in a different way based on our shortcomings last year," said Morgan coach Ross DeMay, now in his 14th season. "They bought in and they grew as the season went on." Morgan has played in 10 championship finals under DeMay. Jayden Gutierrez scored the second goal for Morgan in the 48th minute. item.title: Urban Meyer Doesn’t Hold Back on Ohio State After Upset Loss to USC
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - JANUARY 09: Urban Meyer looks on during a game between the Oregon Ducks and the Indiana Hoosiers in the 2025 College Football Playoff Semifinal at the Chick-fil-A Peach Bowl at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on January 09, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Ohio State lost star quarterback Julian Sayin two weeks ago to what is believed to be a season-ending injury, paving the way for true freshman Luke Fahey to make his first career start. item.title: Darren Agu Earns Second Mountain West Defensive Player of the Week Honor

item.title: Recap: Kadri and Schwartz each score twice; propel Colorado past Chicago
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 02: Jaden Schwartz #71 of the Colorado Avalanche celebrates with Brock Nelson #11 after scoring a goal against the Chicago Blackhawks during the first period at United Center on November 02, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tonight, the Colorado Avalanche took on the Chicago Blackhawks for the first time this season. While the Avs found themselves in a multi-goal deficit early yet again, they would ultimately come away with a 5-2 win. Let’s take a look at all the action from tonight! First Period As previously mentioed, Colorado found themselves in a multi-goal deficet early on in this game, as the Blackhawks scored two goals not even halfway through the period, with the first goal coming not even a minute into the game off of an incredibly fluky play, which saw Cale Makar deflect a shot from Wyatt Kaiser past Mackenzie Blackwood. Shortly after, Roman Kantserov would score on a two-on-one rush off of a Nazem Kadri turnover to make it 2-0, Chicago, as he just put a great shot past Blackwood, and that would be all of the goals that the Blackhawks would score on the night. If there’s one thing that Colorado has historically known how to do, it’s score quickly. That’s exactly what they do before the first period ends, tying the game at 2-2, with two goals just 26 seconds apart. Nazem Kadri redeemed his earlier snafu and scored his first of the night first, as he made an incredible diving play to poke the puck past Spencer Knight and get the Avs on the board. Jaden Schwartz scored just 26 seconds later, as he picked a corner and was able to get the puck past the short-side of Knight to tie the game at 2-2. Second Period Kadri and Schwartz would each score again in the second period to give Colorado a 4-2 lead over Chicago heading into the third period. Kadri’s second goal of the night would come off a deflection on the power play, and Schwartz’s second would also come off of a deflected puck, which just dribbled into the net past Knight with under a minute to go in the period. Third Period The game was essentially over before the final 20 minutes of play even began but Devon Toews would get his fifth goal of the season with an empty netter in this period, for a final score of 5-2. Takeaways After being down 2-0 early in the first period, this game looked like it could have gone the same way that Colorado’s game against Nashville went the other week, where Nashville just ran away with it, and Colorado went away quietly. Of course, the opposite happened here tonight, and I’m glad to see that it did. Instead of going away quietly and not being able to stay composed against a team they should beat, Colorado kept trying, stayed engaged in the game, and were eventually rewarded for their efforts and ended up winning this game, as they should have. The middle six was awesome to watch tonight, with Kadri and Schwartz obviously being the standouts here tonight, each scoring two goals.

item.title: 'On his way': Skip Bayless makes a mid-game prediction about Caleb Williams during Seahawks vs Bears
item.description: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images The Chicago Bears have just picked up a dominant win against the Seattle Seahawks, beating them 34-17 on the road. item.title: Boston Celtics Drop Big Test Against Houston Rockets
item.description: The Boston Celtics saw their five-game winning streak come to an end on Monday night as they fell 109-93 against the Houston Rockets in Houston. With the loss, the Celtics are now 5-2. The Rockets, one of the best teams in the NBA so far, are now 7-1. Here's what you need to know from this loss. What's going on with Payton Pritchard? Yes, Pritchard has had a few games where he excelled, but he's also had a few games where he's really struggled. If this team is going to play win without George, they are going to need Pritchard to be better, and he was very poor in this one.
